want.who_she_is: Cass Ridley, 24. Eighteen months of it belonging to somebody else, four weeks served. A rented room over a laundry on the east side, a monitor on her left ankle, and a job at a hardware and pawn shop because the shop is one of two places in the zone that will sign an hours sheet. What she has to lose: the fourteen months she is not doing — a violation is custody, and the game says so in plain words on the first screen.
want.obligation: Delgado, Tuesdays at two, at the county office, with the sheet due Friday and her signature under his. And a second enforcer that is not a person: the box — a radius drawn around her room, home by eight, and a battery that holds eighteen hours.
want.collector_note: §4a — he holds the obligation and is NOT the pipe the porn comes down. Field collectors carry 0.4-3.8% of a game's explicit passages and are never the top figure. Delgado has ONE surface, at `vouch 60`, and arrives late. The lint `the collector is also the target` reads this.
want.appetite: To be in a room nobody can place her in, and to be wanted while she is in it. It cannot be finished for a structural reason rather than a poetic one: every room she gets into becomes a room she is known in. The box logs a point every sixty seconds, Marty knows her hours, Rae knows when she comes down the stairs, and Delgado has all of it on one page every Tuesday. The appetite renews out of its own successes. WHERE THE HOLD STOPS BEING THE REASON: the week the box comes off, nobody is owed anything by anyone, and at 19:45 she walks the same route to the same back room.
want.ascent: BOTTOM: six streets — her room, the laundry under it, Marty's shop, the county office, the lot behind the shop, the bus stop where the line runs. Home by eight, and every door she walks through is a row in a log somebody else reads on Tuesday. TOP: the far side of the river after midnight, in rooms that are not in any zone, with people who sign her sheet without reading it, and the box on the desk at home saying she is asleep.
want.charge: reversal (primary) + transformation (late, secondary) — every adult in her life holds a signature over her, and the ascent is her collecting those signatures one at a time; each one collected is a person who now has something to lose. The transformation is §2's last line stated as a moment.

why_this_person.npc_tobin: 26, services the boxes out of the county office, bored out of his skull. He holds the only thing she actually wants and treats it as nothing. The cheapest transaction in the game, and she knows it while it is happening.

why_this_person.npc_delgado: The officer. Knows every true thing about her and is scrupulously correct about all of it, which is what makes any slip the loudest event in the game.
